India data centresGo-to-market research for network configuration (NETCONF) tooling

A facility is a data centre building where companies rent space for their routers and switches. The more networks installed in a facility, the more equipment there is to configure, which makes it a stronger prospect for NETCONF tooling. The bar below splits every installed network across the three facility sizes used in this report.

Tenant networks

A tenant network is a company, such as an ISP, a content provider or a carrier, that has its own routers and switches installed inside a facility. Each one is a potential buyer in its own right, separate from the facility operator.

More facilities means more locations with equipment to configure.

Internet exchanges

An internet exchange is a shared switch where many networks connect directly to swap traffic. Each connected network uses a port on that switch, and exchange operators set up and change those connections constantly, so they carry a heavy configuration workload.

Which exchanges are largest?i

Members against total port capacity.

What port speeds do networks buy?

Number of ports at each speed. 10G means 10 gigabits per second.

Exchanges by city

Click a city to filter.

Exchange list

NIXI

The National Internet Exchange of India (NIXI) is the government-backed exchange. It runs connection points, called NOCs, in cities across the country where local ISPs plug in. It matters here for two reasons: NIXI itself is one organisation running many sites, and its ISP lists include regional ISPs that do not appear anywhere in the facility data.

How many of NIXI's ISPs are new to us?i

Every ISP connected at NIXI, checked against the facility and exchange data. Anything outside the first group would be missed by the facility list alone. Click a group to filter.
